description: Raspberry Pi CM5 vision device with an OV9782 global-shutter camera.

page_size_kib.method: KernelPageSize 4 kB measured on a Raze running the PhotonVision image (package c881c60); Buildroot applies BR2_ARM64_PAGE_SIZE_4K after fragments, so every Buildroot-built Raze kernel is 4 KiB. A package build check enforces it

revisions.notes: First-generation Raze boards carry no revision marker. Any board without a marker is gen1; later revisions will be provisioned with one.

rev_source.notes: Gen 1 has no revision marker, so every board reports gen1 (BOARD_DEVICE_REV_DEFAULT). Before the next hardware revision, provision a marker (for example a CM5 OTP customer row or a bootloader EEPROM config key), add the revision here, and ship /usr/lib/board/rev-detect; a missing marker must keep meaning gen1.

serial_source.serial8: last 8 hex digits of the serial

identity.hostname_policy: Default only. Applied at boot as the transient hostname when /etc/hostname is unset or one of the stock names (localhost, localhost.localdomain, buildroot, (none)); never written to /etc. OS-tunable in /etc/board/hostname.env (BOARD_HOSTNAME_POLICY, BOARD_HOSTNAME_PATTERN, BOARD_HOSTNAME_STOCK).

mac_rule.seed: board serial (lowercase hex, as in serial_source)
mac_rule.fallback_seed: "machine-id:" + /etc/machine-id when no serial is readable; with neither, no address is set and the kernel picks random ones. Never a fixed constant.
mac_rule.algorithm: base = 02:b0:b1:b2:b3:b4 where b0..b4 are the first 5 bytes of sha256(seed); host side = base with the last byte XOR 0x01; each interface XORs the last byte of both with its mask

usb_gadget.serial: board serial (first 16 hex digits of /etc/machine-id without one)

network.address: per board: capabilities.gadget-net.addressing (172.31.250.1/24 without a hex serial, or when USB_GADGET_ADDRESS pins one)
network.dhcp_range: the rest of the board's subnet after its address, at most 19 addresses (.2-.6 of a /29)
network.note: USB only: gadget interfaces are bridged with each other, never with Ethernet.

storage_target_evidence: The old Raze bootloader.conf uses boot_partition=/dev/mmcblk0p1 and the PhotonVision Raze cmdline uses root=/dev/mmcblk0p2: the CM5 eMMC (mmcblk0 on a CM5 with eMMC).
Raze images are written over USB with the mass-storage-gadget boot files, which expose the eMMC as a USB disk.
All current Raze boards use CM5 eMMC. A Lite (no eMMC) variant is not planned but not ruled out; it would be a new revision with its own storage_target.
instructions: Hold the boot button on the Raze.
While holding it, connect the Raze's regular USB port (the one used for flashing) to the computer running Atlas, then release the button once the device appears.
The status LED is red while the button is held with power applied. It turns green, and the fan starts, once Atlas begins the USB boot.
The Raze enumerates as 0a5c:2712 (BCM2712 boot ROM). Atlas sends the mass-storage-gadget boot files and the eMMC appears as a USB disk to write the image to.

files.notes: Bootloader image with bootconf.txt embedded. Flash as pieeprom.bin (rpiboot recovery) or pieeprom.upd (in-OS self-update).
rpi-eeprom-digest file (sha256 of the image plus timestamp), not a cryptographic signature. Use as pieeprom.sig.
The configuration embedded in the image, extracted for reference.
rpi-eeprom recovery.bin for BCM2712 from release v2025.12.08-2712, matching the bundled pieeprom. The EEPROM flashing tool rpiboot loads as the second stage. Kept in git (about 100 KB).

fan.control: kernel thermal governor (pwm-fan); lemnosd clients may set a duty, and lemnosd hands the fan back to the governor when it stops

lemnosd.device.method: lemnosd cd72ad0 on a Raze: the pwmfan hwmon fan and cpu-thermal bind and read, and the fan is handed back to the governor when lemnosd stops

pwm.controller.method: fan spins and follows the cooling state on a Raze Gen 1 (image 1.0.10)

pwm.channel.method: fan spins and follows the cooling state on a Raze Gen 1 (image 1.0.10)

pwm.period_ns.method: fan spins and follows the cooling state on a Raze Gen 1 (image 1.0.10); value from the old helios fan blobs

pwm.polarity.method: normal polarity: higher levels run the fan faster on a Raze Gen 1 (image 1.0.10); inverted left it nearly stopped

cooling_levels.method: cooling state 1 at 58 C read back 83 % (212/255) on a Raze Gen 1 (image 1.0.10)

min_level.method: chosen by the user: a 70 % floor keeps air moving

trips_c.method: sysfs on device: Raze running the PhotonVision image (package c881c60, kernel 7.2.9); step_wise governor without polling; trips 50/60/67.5/75 C plus a 110 C critical trip

cooling_device_type.method: sysfs on device: Raze running the PhotonVision image (package c881c60, kernel 7.2.9); the cooling device type is pwm-fan

hwmon_name.method: sysfs on device: Raze running the PhotonVision image (package c881c60, kernel 7.2.9); hwmon name pwmfan, driver pwm-fan; no tachometer (fan1_input reads 0)

lemnosd.notes: board.toml takes count, offset, gpio and the look from here; wire is rgb for a 24-bit wire_format and rgbw for a 32-bit one, direction 1 is cw and -1 ccw.

leds.notes: SK6812-EC20, 24-bit GRB on the wire. The overlay must not pass rgbw; the ws2812-pio-rp1 driver always reads 4 bytes per LED (R, G, B, W) from userspace and drops W. Logical LED i is driver slot (offset + direction * i) mod count, as in HeliOS main.

helper.backend: lemnosd (lemnos-ctl led ..., client raze-leds) when /usr/bin/lemnos-ctl exists, else frames written to the device; BOARD_HW_BACKEND=lemnosd|sysfs chooses
helper.byte_order: rgbw (driver layout, W ignored), RAZE_LEDS_ORDER in /etc/board/raze-leds.env; always four letters (sysfs backend)

part.method: colours correct with the overlay without rgbw on a Raze Gen 1 (image 1.0.10)

wire_format.method: with rgbw (32 bits per LED) the colours smeared around the ring; without it they were correct

userspace.layout.method: raze-leds writing 4 bytes per LED (R, G, B, W) gave correct colours; matches the ws2812-pio-rp1 driver source

gpio.method: the ring lights on a Raze Gen 1 (image 1.0.10)

lemnosd.device.method: lemnosd cd72ad0 on a Raze: the ws2812 ring binds on /dev/leds0 with wire rgb and offset 5, and the progress, updating, breathe and locate effects show correctly

index.offset.method: sysfs on device: Raze running the PhotonVision image (package c881c60, kernel 7.2.9); all 16 LEDs show correct colours with offset 5, the 4-byte rgbw userspace layout and no rgbw overlay flag; HeliOS main uses the same offset

ssh-keys.notes: OpenSSH public keys on the boot partition are added to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys at boot. Nothing is removed and password login is never enabled. Atlas can write the file when it flashes a board.

serial-console.notes: The USB gadget's ACM ports (ttyACM* on the host) give a recovery console that works without networking. Physical access to the port already allows a reflash. An OS turns it off by masking serial-getty@ttyGS0/1.service.

usb-power.control: kernel gpio hogs (raze-usb-power overlay), on at boot
usb-power.power_policy: udev 60-raze-usb-power.rules: power/control=on and USB2 hardware LPM off for every USB device

lemnosd.notes: A gpio-output that lemnosd can switch. While the overlay's hog holds GPIO20 (the default), lemnosd cannot request the line and reports the device missing; an OS that wants runtime control loads the overlay with hog=off.

hardware-service.default_backend: lemnosd when lemnos-ctl is installed, else sysfs (BOARD_HW_BACKEND in /etc/board/hw.env overrides)

addressing.input: the gadget's USB serial (iSerialNumber, the board serial) normalized to Atlas's board-serial rule: all hex, at least 8 digits, the last 8 in lowercase
addressing.algorithm: h = the first 4 bytes of sha256(the 8 ASCII characters) as a big-endian u32; split base into /prefix subnets, drop those inside an exclude range, and take the remaining subnet at index h mod their count (8160), counting up from the lowest. The device has the subnet's first host address; DHCP offers the host the rest.
addressing.fallback: address (above), the fixed address of images before per-board addressing, when the serial gives no subnet or USB_GADGET_ADDRESS pins one; it is excluded from base so old and new boards never share a subnet
addressing.collisions: two boards on one computer share a subnet with probability 1/8160; among k boards about k(k-1)/16320 (0.55% for 10)

select.source: kernel DT, rpi-7.2.y 53679a5: the i2c1-pi5 overlay enables &i2c1, which rp1.dtsi defines as rp1_i2c1: i2c@74000 (snps,designware-i2c) inside rp1 under pcie@1000120000 (rp1_target, bcm2712.dtsi) under /axi
the i2c-gpio overlay's node /i2c@0 is the board's only i2c-gpio adapter

i2c.bus_numbers: Linux numbers buses in probe order: "bus" is the number on the 7.2.9 image, a hint only. Find a bus by its "select" (the keys of a Lemnos i2c: selector: name, compatible, of, node). Other buses on that image: i2c-10, the camera (ov9782 at 0x60); i2c-13 and i2c-14, the HDMI DDC buses (107d508200.i2c, 107d508280.i2c). Nothing else answers on buses 1 and 4.

chip_id.notes: The BMM150 boots suspended (0x4B = 0x00) and reads 0x00 for its id until power control bit 0 is set.

devices.shunt_note: unverified: the user remembers 10 or 20 mOhm; to be settled from the resistor marking (R010 or R020) or a USB-C meter comparison. If it is 20 mOhm, shunt_ohm becomes 0.02 and max_current halves
devices.max_current_source: derived, not a board rating: the INA238's full-scale shunt voltage (163.84 mV) over shunt_ohm, the largest current it can measure (a 0.5 mA current LSB)

chip_id.notes: Manufacturer id "TI" (0x5449). The registers are big-endian, so an SMBus word read (i2cget ... w) returns it byte-swapped (0x4954). Die id: register 0xFF = 0x2381.

buses.method: chip-id register reads on the device (PhotonVision image, package c881c60): the BMI088 answers on the i2c-gpio bus (/dev/i2c-4), the BMM150 and INA238 on the i2c1-pi5 bus (/dev/i2c-1)

devices.method: chip-id register reads on the device (PhotonVision image, package c881c60): accel 0x18 reg 0x00 = 0x1E, gyro 0x68 reg 0x00 = 0x0F, BMM150 0x10 reg 0x40 = 0x32 with 0x4B bit 0 set, INA238 0x40 reg 0xFE = 0x5449 and reg 0xFF = 0x2381

device.method: sysfs on device: Raze running the PhotonVision image (package c881c60, kernel 7.2.9); /dev/watchdog0 is Broadcom BCM2835 Watchdog timer

driver.method: sysfs on device: Raze running the PhotonVision image (package c881c60, kernel 7.2.9); /dev/watchdog0 is Broadcom BCM2835 Watchdog timer

selftest.gadget_reference: identity.usb_gadget and capabilities.gadget-net; the check reads usb-gadget.env on the board

actions.notes: BOARD_ACTIONS in /etc/board/identity.env. A request drops /run/board/requests/<id>; a root path unit runs the action, so the endpoint stays unprivileged.
